newsitem.title: UK: S&P gives Egypt BBB minus long-term rating.
newsitem.headline: S&P gives Egypt BBB minus long-term rating.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Wednesday it had assigned its BBB minus long-term and A3 short-term foreign currency credit ratings to the Arab Republic of Egypt.

S&P said it also assigned its A minus long term and A2 short term local currency credit ratings to Egypt, affecting approximately 34 billion Egyptian pounds ($10 billion) of senior unsecured Egyptian pound denominated treasury bills and bonds.
"The outlook on the long-term ratings is stable," S&P said.

-- A robust commitment to fiscal restraint, underscored by general government deficits of 1.3 pct of GDP annually in fiscals 1994-95 and 1995-96. Targeted at 1.1 pct of GDP in 1996-1997, fiscal deficits should remain modest for the rest of the decade.
-- External debt service (including short-term debt) equivalent to 17 percent of annual exports, among the lowest of similarly rated sovereigns.
-- Accelerating structural reforms, including privatisation, trade liberalisation and deregulation which should further strengthen government finances.
--The deepening political consensus behind economic reform.
"The higher local currency rating reflects Egypt's sound fiscal policies and the central bank's success in lowering inflation and real interest rates at moderate levels going forward," S&P said.
-- Low per capita income, at about $1,200 in 1997, and a still weak social infrastructure that will continue to test the government's commitment to conservative financial policies.
-- A moderately high, although declining, net government debt burden estimated at 53 percent of GDP in fiscal in 1997.

-- Low but improving levels of savings and investment, now at about 18 percent of GDP, which constrain near-term growth prospects, although output should rise by about five percent annually for the rest of the decade.
-- Export earnings still concentrated in petroleum products, tourism and remittances.
